Yes. Above 35°C, the battery wears out faster, so every charge lasts less, for good.

items.text: Out of hot cars and sun

post.title: Does heat hurt your phone's battery?
post.caption:
Does heat hurt your phone's battery? Yes 🔥

Phone batteries are lithium-ion, and they work best between 0 and 35 °C (32 to 95 °F). Above that, heat speeds up the chemistry that wears the battery, so it loses capacity for good: every charge lasts a little less. A car parked in the sun gets much hotter than that. When a phone gets too hot it slows or pauses charging to protect itself. The takeaway, on Android or iPhone: keep it out of hot cars and direct sun, and take a thick case off while it charges.
Send this to the friend who leaves their phone on the dashboard.

sources.note: Apple, Maximizing battery life: iPhone works best at 0-35 °C (32-95 °F) ambient; temperatures above 35 °C can permanently damage battery capacity; charging in high temperatures can damage it further; software may limit charging above 80%; remove certain cases during charging

Apple Support, If your iPhone or iPad gets too hot or too cold: use between 0 and 35 °C; very hot conditions can permanently shorten battery life; don't leave your device in a car; when too warm, charging slows or stops
Apple Support, iPhone battery and performance: avoid charging or leaving your iPhone in hot environments, including direct sun exposure
